challenge_pass.real_objective: Make TheRealSynth/ideabin-ai safe to hand off to ProjectFoundryOS/ideabin-ai later -- without performing the transfer now -- by finding and fixing every reversible place the repository's own content assumes it will always be owned by TheRealSynth, while keeping true historical records true and keeping current product behavior/tests green.
hidden_assumptions: That 'fix migration hazards' means the transfer should be simulated now by writing ProjectFoundryOS into the docs -- rejected, since the transfer has not happened and the mission explicitly forbids performing it.

That every string match for the org name is a hazard -- rejected for the one historical receipt (.agent-results/IDEA-REV-005.json), which is a forbidden_path and a true historical fact, not live configuration.

That this mission owns fixing agent-mission-control's own control/PROJECTS.yaml pointer to ideabin-ai -- rejected: that file lives outside owns_paths, in a different repository, and is the explicit subject of the sibling PFORG-MIG-AMC-005 mission.

That GitHub Actions being absent on main is a transfer-caused hazard -- rejected after checking commit history: it was deliberately removed for the project's PAUSED status one day before this mission, unrelated to migration.
challenge_pass.obvious_path: Grep the repository for every literal occurrence of 'TheRealSynth' and mechanically replace it with 'ProjectFoundryOS' everywhere, then declare the repository migrated.
challenge_pass.optimized_path: Grep the repository for 'TheRealSynth', but only rewrite occurrences that are live configuration/launcher instructions (not historical receipts/PR URLs in forbidden_paths), and only after distinguishing genuinely reversible repository-content hazards from GitHub-account-level hazards (GitHub App scope, Vercel Git integration, local clone remotes) that cannot be fixed by editing files at all.
challenge_pass.non_obvious_path: Instead of swapping one hardcoded org string (TheRealSynth) for another hardcoded org string (ProjectFoundryOS) that is not yet true, remove the org-name dependency from launcher/deployment/promotion-contract prose entirely: point agents/readers at runtime-resolvable identity (git remote / GitHub invocation context) plus a single canonical readiness document, mirroring the repository-registry/alias mechanism the sibling PFORG-MIG-AMC-005 mission is building for the control-plane repository itself.
challenge_pass.cheapest_reversible_test: A full recursive, read-only grep of the repository for 'TheRealSynth', 'github.com', 'vercel.com', and 'supabase.co' across all tracked file types, cross-checked against GitHub's PR/branch API (list_pull_requests) and commit history for hazards invisible to a plain file grep (e.g. CI configuration state, open PRs). Zero write risk, fully discriminates the hazard set before any edit is made.
challenge_pass.alternate_access_surfaces: Used the GitHub API (mcp__github__list_pull_requests, get_commit) in addition to the local git clone to see GitHub-side state not present in file contents: open PR #11 (unrelated, chatgpt/scoring-input-automation-design-v1, docs-only, does not touch migration-relevant files) and the prior day's CI-workflow-removal commit (d166788).
challenge_pass.existing_assets_or_open_source: Reused the sibling PFORG-MIG-AMC-005 mission's chosen mechanism (canonical repository registry / runtime discovery instead of global string replacement) for consistency across the five-repo cohort, rather than inventing an unrelated approach for this repository alone. Reused the existing .agent-results/IDEA-REV-005.json as the structural template for this result file, and AGENTS.md/docs/AI_HANDOFF.md's existing 'resolve current origin/main at runtime, old SHAs are historical evidence only' convention as the precedent for treating repository identity the same way.
challenge_pass.human_in_loop_option: The actual GitHub organization transfer, GitHub App/token re-authorization for the new org, Vercel project (re)connection, and updating remotes on other humans'/machines' existing local clones are all owner-executed or owner-gated actions that cannot and should not be automated by this mission; they are enumerated explicitly as 'Remaining owner actions' in the readiness doc rather than attempted.
challenge_pass.recommendation: Adopted the non-obvious path: removed hardcoded TheRealSynth assumptions from the 4 files where they functioned as live configuration/launcher instructions, left the one historical receipt untouched (forbidden_path + truthful history), and documented account-level hazards that no file edit can fix as explicit owner actions with a post-transfer validation checklist and a fully reversible rollback path.
assumptions_challenged: Rejected writing 'ProjectFoundryOS/ideabin-ai' as present-tense fact into launcher/deployment docs today, since the transfer has not occurred and doing so would itself be false and out of this mission's authority.

Rejected treating the repository's committed files as the complete hazard surface; checked GitHub-side PR/branch/commit state via the API and found the CI-workflow removal and one unrelated open PR that a file-only grep would have missed context for.

Rejected fixing agent-mission-control's control/PROJECTS.yaml ideabin pointer from within this mission; that file is outside owns_paths and is the explicit subject of the sibling PFORG-MIG-AMC-005 mission (state READY, unassigned at time of writing).

Rejected editing the historical receipt .agent-results/IDEA-REV-005.json (contains a TheRealSynth PR URL); it is a forbidden_path and a true historical record, and GitHub preserves such URLs as redirects after a transfer.

route_comparison.route: obvious: global string replace TheRealSynth -> ProjectFoundryOS everywhere
route_comparison.tradeoffs: Fast and simple, but writes a false present-tense fact (the repo is not transferred), silently touches the forbidden historical receipt if run blindly, and still leaves a second doc-edit pass required at the moment of actual cutover.

route_comparison.route: non-obvious (chosen): remove the org-name dependency from live/launcher/deployment prose in favor of runtime-resolved identity + one canonical readiness doc, matching the control-plane repo's own registry/alias approach
route_comparison.tradeoffs: Slightly more editing effort per file and requires readers/agents to resolve identity at runtime instead of reading a literal string, but stays true both before and after the transfer, survives any future rename without another audit mission, and is consistent with the mechanism already chosen for the control-plane repository in PFORG-MIG-AMC-005.

challenge_pass.material_difference: The chosen route changes the actual mechanism, not just the wording: docs go from asserting a single fixed owner/repo string to deferring to a runtime-checkable source of truth (git remote / GitHub invocation context) plus one canonical pointer document. This changes the cost structure (zero additional edits needed at actual cutover or any future rename, versus a guaranteed second edit pass under the obvious route), the workflow (agents self-discover identity instead of trusting prose that can silently go stale during the cohort's staged, mixed-owner transfer window), and keeps the documentation truthful at every point in time rather than only after a transfer that has not happened yet.
challenge_pass.validation_result: Full-repository recursive grep for 'TheRealSynth' found exactly 6 hits before any edit: 5 in live documentation (now fixed) and 1 in the forbidden historical receipt (left untouched by design). A second grep for 'github.com | vercel.com | supabase.co | api.github' found only the same historical receipt's PR URL. After edits, re-running the grep confirms only intentional point-in-time/historical mentions remain (0 unintended hardcoded live assumptions). Confirmed the runtime-discovery mechanism is viable in practice: `git remote -v` and `git rev-parse` were used live in this very session to resolve exact repository identity without any hardcoded string. Ran pnpm install/typecheck/test/build against the edited branch: typecheck clean across all 3 TS packages, 91/91 tests passed, production build succeeded (10 routes). Reverted two incidental tool-generated diffs (pnpm-lock.yaml, apps/web/tsconfig.json) produced merely by running install/build locally, keeping the committed diff scoped to migration-readiness content only.
